facts.claim: Arjun wrote to the Meridian Seed team that Nimbus Labs is raising a seed round to build an AI chief of staff for founders, attached the deck, and asked for a short meeting within the next two weeks.
That ask is open, and the move is theirs: we wait on them.
The mail is one of a wave sent under the same subject; so far no recipient of the wave has replied, bounced or been followed up.
The file has been quiet for less than a day.
The file has no playbook and no stop rule, so nothing says when its quiet would make the work dormant.
This is the first time the founder's history holds Meridian Seed.

inferences.claim: Less than a day after sending, the silence carries no information: the window the founder named is still open.
Meridian Seed is investor work — a fund asked for a first meeting in the seed round — though the brief does not list it among the funds it tracks.
Because no playbook or stop rule covers the file, nothing will bring it back when the two weeks run out; the follow-up date has to be set on purpose.

patterns.claim: In the founder's own numbers for this wave no fund has replied yet — too early to read anything into.

hypotheses.proposition: The mail went to a shared inbox, team@meridianseed.test, that no one partner at Meridian Seed owns.
hypotheses.needs: A reply naming a partner, or a bounce.

hypotheses.proposition: Meridian Seed reads unsolicited decks in batches and answers late, if at all.
hypotheses.needs: Whether a reply comes before the two weeks run out.

unknowns.question: Who at Meridian Seed reads team@meridianseed.test.
unknowns.relevance: A named partner would change who the follow-up goes to and how it is written.

unknowns.question: Whether anyone the founder knows can introduce Nimbus Labs to Meridian Seed.
unknowns.relevance: A warm introduction would beat a second cold mail.

unknowns.question: Whether Meridian Seed backs seed rounds in companies like Nimbus Labs.
unknowns.relevance: If it does not, the right move after the two weeks is to close, not to follow up.

frames.primary: A cold first ask to Meridian Seed for a meeting about the seed round, one fund in a wave, less than a day old — the window the founder set is still open.
rivals: A wave the funds will read as unsolicited and leave unanswered.
Investor work the brief does not track, which will drift with no one deciding to follow up or to close it.

proposed_kind.why: A fund the founder wrote to in the seed round wave, asking for a first meeting; the brief names no kind of work for it.

expected_vs_actual.expected: From the brief's first goal, raising the seed round, and the mail itself: a reply within the two weeks the founder asked for, or one follow-up once they pass.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The mail went out less than a day ago; no reply yet, which at this point means nothing.

scenarios.do_nothing: The two weeks pass and the file goes quiet with no follow-up: the brief does not track this fund and no stop rule will raise it.
scenarios.act: With a follow-up date set for when the two weeks run out, a silent fund gets one short nudge and then a decision to close.
scenarios.best: Meridian Seed replies within the two weeks and a first meeting is booked.
scenarios.worst: No reply and no follow-up, and the fund stays open in the file long after it has quietly passed.
signals_to_watch: A reply or an auto-reply from team@meridianseed.test.
A bounce.
Any fund in the wave replying, which would show the deck reaching readers.
The two weeks the founder named running out with no reply.

reasons: The mail is less than a day old and asked for a meeting within two weeks.
Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and this fund is one of the wave.
Nothing tracks the file: the brief names no kind for it and no stop rule applies.

next_move.what: If the two weeks he asked for pass with no reply, send Meridian Seed one short follow-up.

parsed.alternative: Find a warm introduction to a partner at Meridian Seed and use it in place of a cold follow-up.

parsed.done_when: Meridian Seed has replied and a meeting is set, or the file is closed with its reason after one follow-up.

That ask is open, and the move is theirs: we wait on them.
The mail is one of a wave sent under the same subject; so far no recipient of the wave has replied, bounced or been followed up.
The file has been quiet for less than a day.
